variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Production document extraction turns PDFs, images, and document bundles into structured records that downstream software can safely use. OCR may recover characters, but a production system must also decide which parser to run, whether every required page and field is present, where each value came from, and what to do when evidence is weak or contradictory.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Define the output contract before choosing a model”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Source identity
pairs.detail: Store a content hash, source URI or object key, ingestion time, tenant, page count, and file-validation result.
pairs.explanation: Store a content hash, source URI or object key, ingestion time, tenant, page count, and file-validation result. A retry must point to the same source or declare a new revision.

pairs.label: Typed schema
pairs.detail: Version field names, data types, units, cardinality, required status, table relationships, and normalization rules.
pairs.explanation: Version field names, data types, units, cardinality, required status, table relationships, and normalization rules. Schema migration is separate from model inference.

pairs.label: Evidence anchors
pairs.detail: Keep raw text, page number, text span, polygon or bounding box, and nearby structure for every consequential field.
pairs.explanation: Keep raw text, page number, text span, polygon or bounding box, and nearby structure for every consequential field. A reviewer should be able to inspect the source quickly.

pairs.label: Decision record
pairs.detail: Record parser and model versions, validator results, policy version, review corrections, and the accepted output version.
pairs.explanation: Record parser and model versions, validator results, policy version, review corrections, and the accepted output version. Confidence alone is not a release decision.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. This lesson builds on Document Parsing Systems, which introduces text, layout, tables, and field evidence.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Source identity: Store a content hash, source URI or object key, ingestion time, tenant, page count, and file-validation result. Typed schema: Version field names, data types, units, cardinality, required status, table relationships, and normalization rules. Evidence anchors: Keep raw text, page number, text span, polygon or bounding box, and nearby structure for every consequential field. Decision record: Record parser and model versions, validator results, policy version, review corrections, and the accepted output version.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Route documents with a cheap probe and explicit fallbacks”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Verify the source
pairs.detail: Reject or quarantine corrupt, encrypted, oversized, unsupported, or unsafe files before a parser or renderer handles them.
pairs.explanation: Reject or quarantine corrupt, encrypted, oversized, unsupported, or unsafe files before a parser or renderer handles them.

pairs.label: Split and classify
pairs.explanation: Detect attachments and page ranges. A mixed PDF can contain several document families that need different schemas and owners.

pairs.label: Run the narrowest capable route
pairs.detail: Prefer native text for reliable digital pages, OCR for scans, layout and table models for structural evidence, and specialists for known high-value families.
pairs.explanation: Prefer native text for reliable digital pages, OCR for scans, layout and table models for structural evidence, and specialists for known high-value families.

pairs.label: Fallback on measured evidence
pairs.detail: Escalate unknown layouts, incomplete pages, and failed gates to a stronger route, bounded review, or quarantine.
pairs.explanation: Escalate unknown layouts, incomplete pages, and failed gates to a stronger route, bounded review, or quarantine. Do not silently emit partial records.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. This lesson builds on Document Parsing Systems, which introduces text, layout, tables, and field evidence.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Verify the source: Reject or quarantine corrupt, encrypted, oversized, unsupported, or unsafe files before a parser or renderer handles them. Split and classify: Detect attachments and page ranges. Run the narrowest capable route: Prefer native text for reliable digital pages, OCR for scans, layout and table models for structural evidence, and specialists for known high-value families. Fallback on measured evidence: Escalate unknown layouts, incomplete pages, and failed gates to a stronger route, bounded review, or quarantine.

variants.title: Make the decision
variants.context: Production document extraction turns PDFs, images, and document bundles into structured records that downstream software can safely use. OCR may recover characters, but a production system must also decide which parser to run, whether every required page and field is present, where each value came from, and what to do when evidence is weak or contradictory.
variants.prompt: When should an extracted field become trusted production output?
options: As soon as OCR emits a non-empty string
When its document-level confidence is higher than every other field
After a versioned policy accepts its source evidence, schema, and required validation results
Only after the parser's vendor publishes a benchmark
variants.explanation: Extraction produces a candidate. Trust comes from an action-specific, versioned decision over source identity, evidence, schema, and validation.

variants.prompt: Why are precision and recall usually more useful than one accuracy number for extraction fields?
options: They remove the need for labeled documents
They expose false predictions and missed entities when fields may be optional or repeated
They automatically measure review cost and latency
They are identical for every confidence threshold
variants.explanation: Field schemas contain optional, repeated, and absent labels. Precision and recall make false accepts and misses visible, including their threshold trade-off.
